study type: mixed methods (descriptive survey and qualitative observation)
exposure: physician and patient attitudes towards cesarean delivery
cohort: Obstetric services in six different Shanghai obstetric facilities
finding: High patient volume, limited staffing, societal preference for cesarean delivery, and fear of malpractice charges contribute to the high cesarean delivery rate in Shanghai.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was an efficient way to move patients through the system and was perceived as safer by patients and families, contributing to the high rate.
